reward liability economically sustainable against advertising revenue.

DO NOT START CODING IMMEDIATELY.
First, play:
Snake Puzzle: Slither to Eat
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=puzzle.snakes.puzzle.slithereat.ga
ming

 Snake/worm movement
 Apple mechanics

 Difficulty

 UI

 Sound
 Reward opportunities
 Advertisement flow
Then build your own original implementation.
MOST IMPORTANT REQUIREMENTS
1. GAME NAME
Must come from:
VITE_GAME_NAME=APPLE WORM ADVENTURE
and be accessed through:
GAME_NAME
2. SUGGESTED TECH STACK
The suggested stack is:
MongoDB
Express.js
React.js
Node.js
But:
INTERNS MAY USE THEIR PREFERRED TECH STACK.
The technology choice is flexible.
The required functionality and engineering quality are not.
3. VELoop ECONOMY
This is a rewards and engagement platform.
Therefore, every game developed for this program should think beyond
gameplay.
Build meaningful:
Gameplay
↓
Engagement
↓
Rewarded Ad Opportunity
↓
Verified Ad
↓
Controlled Reward
↓
Wallet / Progress
↓
Retention
The game should monetize through user-choice rewarded advertising, not by
overwhelming players with interruptions.
4. REWARDED FEATURES
At minimum, implement:
Revive
↓
Rewarded Ad
🏆 Double Score
↓
Rewarded Ad
? Double Coins
↓
Rewarded Ad
🎯 Extra Moves
↓
Rewarded Ad
💡 Hint
↓
Rewarded Ad
? Booster
↓
Rewarded Ad
All important rewards must be:
server validated + capped + idempotent + ledgered.
5. ECONOMIC STABILITY
Never design the game around:
"More ads = more rewards."
Design it around:
"More meaningful engagement = more valuable ad opportunities = sustainable
rewards."
The reward amounts, caps, cooldowns, and multipliers must be configurable so
VELoop can tune the economy later based on actual ad revenue, retention, and
user behavior.
BUILD THIS AS A REAL PRODUCT
The evaluator should not feel:
"This is just an internship CRUD project with a small game attached."
The evaluator should feel:
"This is a real VELoop game product with gameplay, engagement,
monetization, rewards, analytics, and a controlled economy."
That is the expected quality bar.
